x: Our first disappointment was the absence of Bert Footer and Bert Shaw from the start owing to indisposition. The skies were leaden, a wind was blowing with gale force, and there was blinding rain and hail when the runners left the pens.
Arthur Penny finished very strongly and Bert Shaw just pipped him for fifth place, which, considering how close he was to the winner, made Arthur doing a very good performance.

Bert Shaw was 6th, Carter 7th, Beer 9th, Morrell 10th, Shields 16th, Walker 18th, Penny 21st, Tobin 22nd, Taylor 23rd, and Jannaway 29th. In the Closed Events, Syd Jarlett, Bill Speaight and Alf Bishop were amongst the prizewinners.
Older members need no introduction to Albert Shaw, but for others it will be of interest to be reminded that just prior to the war, Albert was one of our most consistent milers.
I should be most happy if more of you, especially the half and the one milers who cannot go to Albert Shaw, would make more use of Franz Stampfl.

Syd Warboys increased our lead over the next stretch, and then we ran over successive stages two newcomers, Bert Shaw and Alf Taylor. Both ran well but nevertheless at Hickstead, Polytechnic and Birchfield had made some inroads into our lead.
Close support was given by Micky Walker (33) Bill Rice (40) Albert Shaw (43) and Cecil Penny (70) who had been brought into the team at the last moment.

Jerman was slightly unlucky not to score in a winning team in his 1st 'National'........Our other two runners, Bert Shaw (50) and Mick Walker (65) backed up well, and every one of our runners can look back upon this day of days with pleasure.

All age groups of the Club were represented but I especially noticed those from Alf's earlier days, in the 1930's, Ken O'Kell, Bill and Frank Webb, Tom Carter, Tom Morrell, Albert Shaw, Tom Cotton, Tommy Scrimshaw and many others.
